Senses.Explanation: ‘Constant light before you, a sheer wall ten thousand fathoms high’ joins two images of immediate clarity and uncompromising height. Masters use the pair to press listeners toward direct recognition, then test whether they can answer from where they stand. Liao'an Qingyu follows the mind-settling exchange with this pair, then shifts without warning to Yunmen's fan and a fish struck in the eastern sea. Gulin Qingmao says the line while raising a torch for an abbot's funeral, beside the claim that birth and death are originally clear. Pofeng Puchong sets the pair in a hall address that refuses taking or rejecting the things at hand and asks who can use the twelve hours. Ying'an Tanhua describes a point where the old tactics of blows and shouts have no opening, and the paired images portray that condition. Jianguan Ziyi says the line in a hall address, draws one stroke with his whisk, and asks why a person with clear eyes still falls into a well. The following question keeps the strong image from becoming a stopping point.

Senses.Note: Dongshan describes an unnamed “thing” that is always present in activity yet cannot be seized through that activity. In the fruit-table case he asks where the fault lies; a senior monk says it lies in activity, and Dongshan has the fruit removed. Later masters use the pair to ask what can actually be recognized now. Wanru and Foyuan raise whisks, Baichi presses the fruit question again, Hefeng adds a verse, and Pufu turns the exchange into a fresh encounter. The pair points to the gap between use and possession, not to a separate object waiting to be found.

Senses.Explanation: A traveler's stance — always on the road — set at the root by Linji over who deserves the offerings, and walked, blown, and beaten through hall addresses, farewell teas, and mountain gates from the Ming retreats to the Qing hermitages. The root sits in Linji Yixuan's own instruction, raised in the Guxue Zhe record: one person always on the road, never leaving home; one person always at home, never leaving the road — which of the two deserves the offerings of gods and men? and Dahui's cry: the thief's body already bared; Baiyu Jingsi, at the Yongfeng hermitage hall, brings the pair down past the buddhas' groping: brow-eye open and the thread underfoot snapped, tipping the Dipper, stepping round the Southern Star, swords hung at the eyebrows, the ferry ridden across the Silver River — and yet one more person: always on the road, never leaving home; never leaving home, always on the road — name him; a look right and left, a shout, the seat left empty; and Yingshan Zhiyin, at the farewell tea before the assembly: this monk coming never left Boshan, going never left Gushan — the dragging-through-mud crowd, feelings unbroken, consciousness-waves undried, gripped and parted, grieving the parting — has no one seen the entering mountain lord: coming, coming, truly not coming — travel well on the road; going, going, truly not going — come to no harm on the way; know the lord's meaning and you know this seat of mine: never out of the ten-foot room, yet always on the road; never off the road, yet always in the room — the moon prints a thousand rivers and never went; the mirror holds ten lands and never came. Guantao Daqi, at the small assembly, walks the old pilgrims through it: Xuefeng three times up Touzi, nine times up Dongshan; Zifu saw the pole-tip from afar and turned straight back — the walkers run the world to death and never leave home; the sitters sit the world to death and are always on the road; had this monk been there — thirty blows for the lot; have you not heard: cloud and thunder escort; Yuan'an Liao, closing the retreat: frost congealed, water frozen — then it knotted; sun warm, wind mild — now it loosens; know this news and you are always on the road, never leaving home; always at home, never leaving the road — the three rafters overhead are the hundred cities' waters, shoulder-bag and bowl no different from feet folded on the cushion — so the knitting was thus, and the loosening thus; not thus, and the cloud goes home to the emperor's city, the water runs off the Jiang and the Han; and Meixi Fudu, leaving the monastery, mounts the seat: the walker's bearing is like a crane, like a cloud — to stay is to stay, to go is to go; staying: pines to eat, ravines to drink, leaves to write on, stones to sit on; going: a hat to wear, clouds to drape, hills to watch, waters to play over — tell me, how far apart are walking and staying?; get it and you get it: never leaving home, always on the road; always on the road, never leaving home — and if not: two straw sandals fierce as a tiger, one bamboo staff alive as a dragon — the staff across the shoulder, down from the seat.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB388.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yikui of Shending. Yikui Yuankui raises a case in which the Buddha sits silently, refuses to teach while two rule-breaking monks remain, and still refuses after Ananda has them removed. The Buddha then says he will not teach people limited to the two lesser paths and leaves his seat. Yikui describes Ananda's strenuous efforts and the assembly left staring, then asks whether the departure nevertheless helps anyone. Senses.Explanation: A remembered Jiangnan spring answers a question about speech and silence. The call of a partridge and the scent of flowers make the reply an immediate scene. Later masters reuse the pair in live answers to different questions and test whether its force can travel.

Senses.PreferredTarget: I often recall Jiangnan in the third month, where partridges call amid the fragrance of a hundred flowers
AlternateTargets: I remember Jiangnan in spring: partridges calling where flowers fill the air with scent
SearchAliases: Jiangnan third month partridge flowers Chan
Senses.Note: Fengxue first answered a question about avoiding speech and silence with this spring scene: Jiangnan in the third month, partridges calling amid flowers. Guxue revoices it to answer a fresh question about sound, while Xiuye uses it at an incense offering. Jizong, Wanfeng, and Wumen each comment on Fengxue's old answer, with Wanfeng expressly warning against settling in sound and color. The remembered scene works as a response in a Chan exchange, not merely a nostalgic landscape description.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 穿卻。雖然，到者裏始好喫山僧痛棒在。其或未然，有寒暑兮促君壽，有鬼神兮妒君福。示項翰林夫人示項翰林夫人禪學者，悟門也，非四禪、八定、五度、九次之別，惟洞明心性，了脫生死，得大自在者之門徑也。古人云：我此門中，不論禪定解脫，祗圖見性。又云：參禪須求玅悟，若不玅悟，無由出離生死大海。今時道流，謬以口耳哄弄閨閣，不求玅悟而脫生死，祗益滑稽，謗大般若，以致埋沒己靈，辜負先聖，可不哀邪？汝既皈依山僧，希求大道，急將明昧兩岐與我一時坐斷，單提一箇話頭，直下不起二念，猛著精神，一蹋到底，千聖齊立下風，萬靈咸希至化，豈不慶快生平也哉？嗟乎！驢鞍橋本非阿爺下頷，水泡沫豈是輪王頂髻？參須真參，悟要實悟，至發明後，更能操守保護，乃為道器。示張黃甫徐仰齋二居士示張黃甫、徐仰齋二居士山河大地、明暗色空、日月星辰、森羅萬象，迷者認為外物，悟者消歸自己。一切時中若能無事於心、無心於事，自然物我一如，隨處自在。不見僧問風穴：「語默涉離微，如何通不犯？」穴云：「常憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百華香。」居士若向者裏開得隻眼，不但世法佛法一念圓融，即風穴老子亦一時收下。到者裏，山河大地、明暗色空、日月星辰、森羅萬象向甚麼處著？居士試道道看。示葉素旃居士示葉素旃居士常住真心，覿體全彰，擬思即錯，動念即乖，十方三世，了無差別。知此者謂之大智，行此者謂之大行，示此者謂之大慈，廣此者謂之大悲，百千三昧皆由此出。奈何眾生迷此，蔽慧日於欲海，埋智劍於塵封，處處貪著，頭頭滯礙，豈知水月鏡像而無體，空華陽燄以非真？莫道凡情不可執，直饒聖號亦是假。居士但當掀翻窠臼，撒手承當，直登解脫之場，大播廣長之舌，攪長河為酥酪，變大地作黃金，始不負山僧之厚望也。勉之。示鎮江賀夫人示鎮江賀夫人寶劍眉間挂，摩尼掌上陳，玻璃拈起處，栗棘一時吞。會得箇中意，日午打三更，一椎擉瞎摩醯眼，鼻孔依然搭上唇。參。示超震禪人示超震禪人雲收雨過，氣肅天高。須彌盍北斗，日月杖頭挑。不是摘蘆江上客，千山萬水路迢迢。踢翻福建飛鳶嶺，蹋斷天台滑石橋。有意氣時添意氣，不逍遙處也逍遙。示張超霞道人示張超霞道人鶯老華殘春已去，風清竹翠夏還來。一輪寶鑑當空照，萬里長空絕點埃。正與麼時，打失香嚴鼻孔，刺瞎靈雲眼睛。且道眉毛還有罪過也無？幾度黑風翻大海，未曾聞著釣舟傾。示王士英夫人示王士英

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 生滅滅已，寂滅為樂。黃面老子四十九年、三百餘會，末後供出死欵，後代兒孫隨邪逐惡，無一箇與他出氣。今日翠巖遠孫番欵去也。卓拄杖一下：吽！吽！謝九溪和尚上堂：春山疊亂青，春水漾虗碧。不知天地間，更有誰相識？師云：大眾，大小雪竇祖師孤陋寡聞，只知有己。翠巖又且不然，春山疊亂青，春水漾虗碧。寥寥天地間，滿眼皆相識。且道知心是什麼人？堪咲九溪留不住，却來洪井涌波濤。謝，秉拂，上堂。一切佛世尊，皆說一乘道。今此一眾，皆應除疑惑。釋迦老子二千年前全機獨露，可惜無人，以至五千退席。後代兒孫雖則不眾，多是當面蹉過。所以道：要明恁麼事，須是恁麼人。大眾！要明恁麼事麼？問取堂中第一座。清明，上堂。三月清明節禁烟，桃華帶雨倍鮮妍，皆言當日靈雲悟，咲破禪和口半邊。眾中莫有為靈雲作主底麼？我且問你，那裏是他不疑處？上堂：今朝三月初十，擊鼓禪徒畢集。欲知時節因緣，雨落堦頭便濕。會即各自歸堂，不會何勞久立。上堂，舉：僧問風穴和尚：語默涉離微，如何通不犯？穴云：常憶江南三月裏，鷓鴣啼處百華香。師云：大眾！風穴和尚只知開口，不覺話墮。今日忽有人問翠巖：語默涉離微，如何通不犯？卓拄杖一下。上堂：百丈有三訣，喫茶珍重歇。翠巖不學百丈，𦘕蛇添足。擊拂子。上堂，舉：資福示眾云：隔江望見剎竿便回去，脚跟下好與三十棒，何況過江來？纔有僧出眾，福云：不堪共語。便歸方丈。師云：資福放處較危，収來太速。若是翠巖又且不然，望見剎竿便回去，有棒不打這般鈍漢；縱然過江來，者棒亦不打這般鈍漢。眾中忽有人道：望見剎竿便回去則且從，過江來為甚麼也不打這般鈍漢？但向他道：却許你具一隻眼。赴黃龍辭眾上堂，舉大愚和尚示眾云：翠巖路嶮𡾟，舉步涉階梯，更有洪源水，滔滔在嶺西。師云：大眾！大小祖師坐在這裏，無門即不然，翠巖絕嶮𡾟，元不涉階梯，去來無窒礙，彼此更何疑？珍重洪源湖海眾，箇中不隔一毫𨤲。再住黃龍禪寺語錄再住黃龍禪寺語錄侍者法孜錄三門。無門為法門，三關何用立。熟處既難忘，又從這裏入。佛殿靈山，一會泥團土塊。問訊燒香，和贜捉敗。方丈。熱喝麤拳，佛來也打。臨濟德山，一時擒下。拈帖。不是護身符，亦非斷貫索，直饒鼻孔遼天，也被這箇穿却。無門老漢還免得麼？却請維那下箇注脚。拈疏。讚嘆無門也是這箇，罵詈無門也是這箇，文彩未彰誰辨得？却煩首座通消息。法座。不動

Addressing practitioners who seek awakening, Qiyuan Xinggang says that direct realization may break a knot of doubt at once, but those who attain something through gradual cultivation especially risk taking a small glimpse for completion.
